differences.title: 1. STORAGE & RETENTION
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar persists messages in per-topic log segments managed by the broker tier, and can tier storage across local and remote media. Retention is enforced by segment retention policies and compaction settings.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream stores messages inside durable streams using per-stream storage with internal indexing, plus periodic snapshots. Retention is governed by stream limits (max age/size/messages) and deletion of expired segments.

differences.title: 2. DELIVERY SEMANTICS
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar supports multiple subscription types (exclusive/shared/failover) with configurable acknowledgment behavior. Redelivery is driven by consumer ack deadlines and replay from the persisted log using subscription cursor state.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream uses consumer acknowledgments and redelivery based on ack policy and delivery attempt state. Consumers maintain delivery sequences, and unacked messages are retried after configured timeouts.

differences.title: 3. CONSUMER TYPES & SCALING
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar subscriptions model fan-out and scaling via shared consumers or partitioned topics, where each consumer independently advances a subscription cursor. Failover subscriptions coordinate active consumers across brokers.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream provides durable consumers that can be push or pull. Scaling is achieved by creating multiple consumers or partitions via stream settings, while each consumer tracks its own sequence and ack state.

differences.title: 4. CLUSTER TOPOLOGY & COORDINATION
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar separates responsibilities: brokers handle protocol and dispatch, while managed metadata and coordination rely on ZooKeeper/BookKeeper style components. Partitioned topics map to broker-led routing with stateful cursors.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream runs within the NATS ecosystem with a lightweight control/coordination path. Stream metadata and consumer state are maintained in JetStream, leveraging NATS’ clustering to route publish/subscribe operations efficiently.

differences.title: 5. ORDERING & PARTITIONING
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar preserves ordering within a topic partition by assigning producers to partitions consistently. Consumers read from partitions, so ordering guarantees are scoped to each partition log and not across the whole topic.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream preserves ordering within a stream by assigning each message a sequence number. If you need higher parallelism, you typically create multiple streams or consumers rather than relying on Kafka-like partition rebalancing.

differences.title: 6. BACKFILL, REPLAY, & OFFSETS
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar enables replay by configuring subscription start positions, including time-based or message-ID based seeking depending on retention. Offset-like cursor positions advance as consumers ack, supporting deterministic rewinds.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream consumers define their starting point (e.g., from the last acknowledged message, specific sequence, or from the earliest retained message). Delivery uses consumer state plus stream retention boundaries to enable controlled backfill.

differences.title: 7. OPERATIONS & EFFICIENCY PROFILE
differences.leftDesc: Pulsar’s multi-component architecture (brokers, topic ownership, partitioning, and metadata coordination) offers powerful features but requires careful tuning of partitions, batching, and cursors for optimal latency and throughput under load.
differences.rightDesc: JetStream is designed to run as an add-on streaming layer for NATS, often resulting in simpler operational footprints for teams focused on low-latency publish/consume with durable streams and straightforward ack/redelivery tuning.
